Definition: from G575 and εἶμι (to go); to go away:--go. Compare G548.
BiblicalUsage: To be away, or to go away — the brethren sending Paul and Silas away by night from Berea, Paul writing that whether present or absent he is the same man, and his joy that even though absent in body he is present in spirit with the Colossians. Distance changes the body, not the bond.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word comforts every separated church: Paul's absence did not break his care. Distance never broke the bond the gospel made, and I hold that the same gospel binds believers across any distance.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
